q: How does an NBFC calculate financed emissions for two-wheeler and commercial vehicle loans?
title: Financed emissions for vehicle loans
short: Under PCAF, a motor vehicle loan's financed emissions are the vehicle's annual emissions times an attribution factor: the outstanding loan amount divided by the vehicle's total value at origination. Vehicle emissions come from fuel used, or from distance and fuel economy, multiplied by a fuel factor. Most NBFC books start with estimated data.
audience: Vehicle finance NBFCs and lenders in India and South Asia

sections.h: The formula PCAF uses for motor vehicle loans
ol: Attribution factor = outstanding loan amount / total vehicle value at origination. The denominator stays fixed for the life of the loan, so the factor falls as the borrower repays.
Vehicle emissions = litres of fuel used in the year x the fuel's emission factor. If fuel is unknown, litres = kilometres driven / fuel economy in km per litre.
Financed emissions = attribution factor x vehicle emissions. Add up across all loans and report the total with its data quality score.
p: The motor vehicle loans asset class in the PCAF Global GHG Accounting and Reporting Standard, Part A (second edition, 2022) covers loans taken to buy a vehicle, for consumers and businesses. A general working capital loan to a transporter falls under business loans instead.

ul: Better scores (1 and 2): actual fuel consumption, or actual distance with the fuel economy of the known make and model.
Middle score (3): known make and model, with estimated distance.
Weaker scores (4 and 5): only the vehicle type, or nothing specific, with average distance and average fuel economy.
p: Most Indian vehicle loan books will sit at score 4 or 5 in the first year, because the lender records make, model and price but not kilometres. Say so in the disclosure and show how you plan to improve it, for example by collecting odometer readings at service or renewal.

sections.h: Choices that change the answer most
ul: Annual kilometres. A commercial vehicle may run five to ten times more than a private car or scooter. Use segment averages, not one figure for the whole book.
Fuel economy. A two-wheeler and a light goods vehicle differ several times over. Keep a table by vehicle type and fuel.
Fuel type. Use the matching IPCC 2006 default: diesel 2.68 kg CO2 per litre, petrol 2.31 kg CO2 per litre, CNG 2.75 kg CO2 per kg.
Electric vehicles. PCAF counts the electricity used for charging as the vehicle's emissions; estimate kWh from distance and apply the grid factor, 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for India.
Vehicle value. Use the on-road value recorded at origination, the same figure across reporting years.

sections.h: What to put in the disclosure
p: State the asset class, the number of loans and outstanding amount covered, the method for distance and fuel economy, the emission factors and their source, and the weighted data quality score. These are CO2 figures from fuel combustion only; say so if you do not add methane and nitrous oxide.

example.title: Worked estimate: two loans
lines: Light diesel goods vehicle: Rs 6 lakh outstanding on a Rs 10 lakh vehicle, attribution 6 / 10 = 0.6
12,000 km a year / 15 km per litre = 800 litres; 800 x 2.68 = 2,144 kg CO2
Financed: 0.6 x 2,144 = 1,286 kg, about 1.29 t CO2
Petrol two-wheeler: Rs 40,000 outstanding on an Rs 80,000 vehicle, attribution 0.5
8,000 km a year / 45 km per litre = 177.8 litres; 177.8 x 2.31 = 410.7 kg CO2
example.note: Distance and fuel economy here are assumptions, so these are score 4 or 5 figures. Replace them with actual readings as you collect them.

senseible: Senseible does not calculate financed emissions for a loan book. It reads fuel invoices, so a transport borrower can give its lender documented litres of diesel or petrol instead of an estimate, which improves the data quality score for that loan.
